passages.context: At IV d.17 c.3 nn.4-6, Lombard transmits penitential teaching that directs the penitent to present his life to God through a priest, to anticipate divine judgment by confession, and to obey Christ's command that those being cleansed show themselves personally to priests. The passage treats confession as an ecclesial act of humiliation and reconciliation and concludes that priests can profit and spare those who confess. This establishes Lombard's positive reception of priestly confession; its quoted authority is the medieval De vera et falsa poenitentia transmitted under Augustine's name, not an authenticated work of Augustine.
passages.notes: Read directly at printed pp. 349-350. Number 4 begins on p. 349 and continues on p. 350; number 5 begins on p. 349; number 6 is on p. 350. The passage supports Lombard's priest-directed penitential synthesis. It does not by itself supply the necessity exception, prove Augustinian authorship of the embedded quotation, define the sacrament's complete later scholastic theology, or state current canon law. Read IV d.17 c.4 n.3 for the explicit distinction between priestly ministry and impossibility.

passages.context: At IV d.17 c.4 n.3, Lombard says one should seek a priest able to bind and loose. If no priest is available, the penitent may confess to a neighbor, who has no power of absolution; the penitent is nevertheless said to become worthy of pardon through desire for the priest. Lombard then invokes the ten lepers, cleansed while going to show themselves to the priests, and states that God regards the heart when necessity prevents arrival. Number 4 continues the ecclesial and priestly reading while distinguishing private from public disclosure.
passages.notes: Read directly at printed pp. 351-352. Number 3 begins on p. 351 and continues through the opening of p. 352; number 4 follows on p. 352. Luke 17:14 is cited in the edition's footnote to the leper sentence. This passage supports a carefully bounded synthesis: priestly confession is to be sought, the non-priest does not absolve, and necessity does not frustrate pardon where desire for the priest remains. It does not state that desire alone completes the sacrament, that lay confession supplies sacramental absolution, or that the lepers' historical cleansing was itself sacramental penance. The quoted material is from De vera et falsa poenitentia transmitted under Augustine's name, not authenticated Augustine.

work.author: Peter Lombard
work.description: Peter Lombard's four-book Latin theological synthesis. Its fourth book treats the sacraments; distinction 17 discusses contrition, confession, satisfaction, and the relation between priestly ministry and necessity.
